title: Silas and the Promise
premise: Marine biologist Paloma Okafor has spent five years in the coastal town of Merrow Point rebuilding after a betrayal, measuring her days in turtle nests and tide charts. When a storm-damaged post office box yields a letter Silas Reyes wrote her eleven years ago — a letter that never arrived, explaining the truth behind the night she fled — she must decide whether the past deserves a second hearing. Silas returns to town as the consultant whose development project threatens the very reef she's spent years protecting, forcing them onto opposite sides of a public fight even as old feelings reignite. In the end, Paloma exposes the developer's falsified environmental data, Silas walks away from the career that once cost him everything, and the two of them catch the last ferry of the season together, choosing truth and each other over safety and silence.
about_author: Coral Dunmore is the pen name of a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set where the land runs out of excuses. She lives on a windswept peninsula with a rescue dog named Buoy and a stubborn belief in second chances.

chapters.title: What the Storm Left
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. After a nor'easter, the old post office clears out damaged boxes, and Paloma is handed a water-stained letter postmarked eleven years ago — in Silas's handwriting, addressed to her. She can't bring herself to open it. Emotional beat: the past knocking with wet hands.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with a flashback. She finally reads the letter: Silas never betrayed her that night in college; he was protecting her from his father's schemes. Rage and grief arrive together, five years of healing reframed as a misunderstanding. Emotional beat: the ground shifting.

chapters.title: The Man on the Ferry
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The seasonal ferry brings a new environmental consultant to assess the marina expansion — and it's Silas, older, guarded, clearly unaware she lives here. Their first conversation is civil, loaded, and brief. Emotional beat: recognition like a bruise pressed.

chapters.title: Silas
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He took the Merrow Point contract to prove he builds clean projects, haunted by his father's corrupt legacy and the girl he lost protecting her from it. Seeing Paloma on the dock upends his plan. Emotional beat: hope he doesn't trust.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Town council meeting: Paloma speaks against the marina expansion; Silas defends it professionally. They agree to a tense truce — he'll walk the reef with her before finalizing his report. Emotional beat: adversaries circling the same water.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The reef walk: she shows him the nesting grounds the development would destroy, and old intimacy surfaces in shared shorthand — he still remembers her field notes style. They argue about the letter's eleven lost years. Emotional beat: anger braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Version He Told Himself
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confronts why he never searched for Paloma after college — shame, his father's threats, and a cowardice he's never named. He drafts a message to her and deletes it. Emotional beat: the slow cost of self-deception.

chapters.title: Nest Nine
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A storm threatens a vulnerable turtle nest; Paloma and Silas work through the night relocating eggs, soaked and laughing despite themselves. Something unclenches between them. Emotional beat: the body remembering trust before the mind permits it.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Her sister visits and challenges her: is Paloma's careful life healing, or a fortress? Paloma admits the letter cracked something she'd sealed over. She agrees to let Silas explain in full. Emotional beat: choosing to be brave in small doses.

chapters.title: What Actually Happened
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Silas tells the whole story of that night — his father's fraud, the threat to Paloma's scholarship, the choice he made alone. Paloma grieves the eleven years but sees the boy inside the man. Emotional beat: truth as a door, not a wound.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A near-kiss on the bluff after the town's harvest festival; interrupted by a call — Silas's firm has fast-tracked the marina approval, his reef concerns overruled. The spell breaks. Emotional beat: joy interrupted by the old machinery of duty.

chapters.title: The Report
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas discovers his firm's client submitted falsified baseline environmental data — and his name is on the report. His career, rebuilt brick by brick, is now the instrument of the thing he swore never to do. Emotional beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Loyalty
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. His firm's partner pressures him to stay quiet, invoking loyalty and the career that 'saved' Silas from his father's ruin. Silas recognizes the same choice, eleven years older. Emotional beat: history offering a rerun.

chapters.title: What Paloma Saw
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma's own data shows anomalies matching the falsified baseline. She realizes Silas may have signed it — or may be trapped. Old betrayal reflex fires; she confronts him coldly in front of colleagues. Emotional beat: the fortress rebuilding itself.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas copies the firm's internal files and drives through the night to Merrow Point, intending to confess and hand her everything — then loses his nerve and instead asks her to trust him one more time without proof. She refuses. Emotional beat: love asking for what fear won't give.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The final autumn ferry approaches; Silas is due to leave, contract done, silence intact. Paloma rereads the eleven-year-old letter and understands he's repeating the same solitary sacrifice. She runs for the dock. Emotional beat: the choice made with her feet.

chapters.title: The Dock
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the dock, Silas hands her the files before she can speak — he'd already decided to blow the whistle. They say the things eleven years and five years each kept unsaid. Emotional beat: two people finally standing in the same truth.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The whistle blows: the marina project collapses, Silas loses his firm and his professional standing, and Merrow Point divides over the scandal. Paloma stands publicly beside him. Emotional beat: the price of truth, paid together.

chapters.title: What the Reef Keeps
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The nesting grounds are granted protection; Paloma leads the first volunteer survey of the off-season, Silas at her side with no title and no agenda. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: A Letter Worth Waiting For
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas writes Paloma a new letter — not an apology or an explanation, but a promise — and gives it to her unsealed. She reads it aloud on the bluff. Emotional beat: words that finally arrive on time.

chapters.title: Spring Ferry
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. Spring returns; the first ferry of the new season carries visitors to a town that kept its reef, and Paloma and Silas count the season's first nest together. She no longer measures her life in small safe steps. Emotional beat: home is a person, finally claimed.
